saints.name: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The Jewish philosopher Edith Stein, who became a Carmelite nun and died at Auschwitz, a co-patroness of Europe…
biography: Edith Stein was born into a devout Jewish family at Breslau in 1891 and became a distinguished philosopher, a student and assistant of Edmund Husserl. Reading the autobiography of St. Teresa of Ávila brought her to the Catholic faith, and she was baptized in 1922, later entering the Discalced Carmelites at Cologne under the name Teresa Benedicta of the Cross.

As Nazi persecution intensified she was moved for safety to a Carmel in the Netherlands, but after the Dutch bishops publicly condemned Nazi racism the regime arrested Catholics of Jewish descent in reprisal. She was deported and killed in the gas chambers of Auschwitz on 9 August 1942, offering her life for her people.
saints.knownFor: Uniting Jewish heritage, philosophy, and Carmelite martyrdom.

canonization.canonized: 1998 by Pope John Paul II; co-patroness of Europe (1999)

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (vatican.va)
